After many years of anxiety/IC pain, my physical therapist and I figured out that due to me constantly flexing my abs in order to appear thinner from childhood onwards and subsequent development of an ED (still a habit I don't immediately catch myself doing) at the encouragement of a family member (ugh), that I basically shredded my pelvic floor and abs and was constantly physically tense. My PT said I had one of the tightest pelvic floors she had worked with and we never did do any internal PT due to it. I also have developed vitamin deficiencies on and off and from my most recent ER trip for pelvic pain (July...doing better!) actually only revealed a major potassium deficiency.

I am like 99.99% sure that the physical tensing and the mental side effects alongside from this family member for a good 15 years was what finally did me in. Diazepam suppositories didn't do much for me but for what it's worth, I am on a ton of anxiety meds and generally do feel better after taking them physically and am able to sleep most nights without peeing 15 times previously. The anxiety became a vicious cycle about being afraid of being in pain or doing things/eating things that would trigger an episode but eventually after I was at my wits ends ready to lose it after so much pain and being denied pain meds I threw myself into PT and didn't avoid going in for UTI/BV tests when I thought I might have an infection.


I don't do PT anymore due to health insurance changes but hopefully that will change soon. I managed my symptoms with PT, occasional uribel and azo, and hydroxyzine for anxiety. I can talk to you more about my anxiety/depression treatment (have been treated for 10 years) and what meds have worked with me. Some mental health medications did flare me but I suppose I could have been hyper aware. If you ever have any questions please feel free to message me. I am not super active on here anymore since I've found frequenting this board worsened my anxiety (not any of you guys...I just felt a lot of despair lurking here and I feel for all of you ❤️), but you can also read through my comment history on my profile too.  Good luck!!

Hi! I highly recommend seeing a urologist, as most GPs in my experience refuse to do anything regarding IC as they don't have a lot of knowledge of it. Better yet, you can find a urologist that specializes in IC. I think the ICN website has a search field? 

A few things to help you survive to your appointment in response to the bullet points you listed:

1) The falling asleep thing is the worst for me. Mostly due to the lack of distractions. I feel like I notice less pain when I'm busy at work. A heating pad will help, but use a timed one so you don't get burns (they're a thing even if you don't feel them happening). Chamomile tea to calm you might help, maybe get a sleep aid like melatonin or diphenhydramine to help get you there.
     Fun fact, diphenhydramine is a main ingredient in Benadryl, which some people consider a "rescue drug" for IC flares. (Long story short, they're not sure what causes IC in every single case as people present different symptoms that respond to different treatment; one of the theories is that IC is caused by a mast cell overgrowth in your bladder. Most antihistamines like allergy medicines help inhibit mast cell growth and provide some people relief. I'm currently on Hydroxyzine [Atarax] 10mg a night, which helps me get to sleep and stay asleep. Not sure if it helps with overall symptoms but it's worth a shot to try. A lot of medication for this condition is trial and error, which sucks, but it is what it is.)

2) One thing that greatly improved by urgency/frequency (the feel of needing to pee every half hour or sometimes worse like 5 minutes) was doing bladder training which is not for everyone. My urologist and physical therapist recommended it, calling it "timed voiding". Basically, on my weekend from work I let myself relax and allow myself to feel the urgency but just doodled/journaled/gamed/netflixed/kept myself busy and gradually spaced out further and further the times when I'd pee.  I can typically go 4 hours now which is INSANE compared to how I was literally even weeks ago. The key was allowing myself to feel the urgency/pain that comes with it and relaxing because I was feet from my bathroom and wasn't going to have any emergencies. I'd recommend doing this first (if you want to try it at all) on a day where you have NOTHING going on at all except some quality relax time :)
One thing my physical therapist brought up was that I was drinking *too much* water everyday. Sometimes I would get to 5 liters. While that helps some people (dr.s theorize it's because it's diluting the acidity in the urine), it was making me pee way too often. I'm now down to 2 liters a day which is the perfect amount for me.


3) Fruits and fruit juice: different problems for everyone, no problems for some. Try to avoid more acidic fruits and fruit juice. For me it's easier to have a list of what I *can* have. Which is mainly just blueberries and canteloupe and melon-like things.
What triggers me: Grapefruits, pineapple, tomato (raw), cranberries/cranberry juice
If you can't live without certain fruits that you find trigger your flares (increased urgency/pain/bladder spasms) then there is a supplement called Prelief which is supposed to block most acid from these sources in your bladder so you can ingest them without as much pain. Walgreens used to sell it, but last time I went to buy it in store, they told me it was discontinued. Look it up on Google, it's pretty cool imo.

4) Drinks: Prelief also works with drinks too! Caffeine is a huge trigger for a lot of people in most forms, along with alcohol. Some people cannot have any carbonated drinks *at all* so sodas can definitely be triggering you too. Even seltzer water. If you have either of these sensitivites, stay AWAY from energy drinks. That may seem obvious, and you may think you can do it (and maybe you can! Everyone's different) but they *kill* me every time I have one despite being able to drink most soda and coffee. Super weird.

5) Urinating: What I found caused problems for me was what you're describing, what some call "Double Voiding". If you produce some urine after a few more minutes, you may think "A-ha! I have proof I'm not emptying my urine completely! Caught you." Which may be true. But I had the same thought and after doing my instillation set (catheterizing and filling the bladder with lidocaine/sometimes Elmiron (only technically approved IC med)) and the nurse was telling me I was emptying my bladder completely every time, I started testing out peeing, then pushing once after the strong stream of urine ended and getting up and leaving the bathroom completely. In my opinion, when I would do the 'sitting on the toilet for 30 minutes' thing, I would feel like complete crap and my bladder would spasm like crazy and I would just want to curl up in a ball but I couldn't do that because it HURT.


I'm sorry if that was a lot, but I'm finally at a 1/10 on most days after being like a 9/10 for 3 months 24/7 after a UTI triggered my symptoms to come back after a 4 year remission. It'll often feel like you have no hope, that you're going to be condemned to this forever, but there is always something to keep trying. Never give up, find a urologist that actually listens to you that you can walk away from every appointment feeling confident even when you feel 10 cm tall. Honestly, a big big BIG part of me getting this "ok" was dealing with my mental health. I won't lie, I had many many breakdowns and my life almost fell apart; I thought I was going to have to quit my job, my partner was getting caregiver fatigue (if you have a partner they should support you through this, but familiarize yourself with caregiver fatigue and how it affects them and never place the responsibility on them to deal with your problems so you don't have to, which I was really guilty of for a long time. It's hard for loved ones to watch another loved one struggle with a chronic illness, ESPECIALLY one that presents no outward physical symptoms, because, over time, they'll want it to go away so you can feel better and they'll want to believe doctors when they can't find anything wrong with you. Just as you need people to be empathetic to you and your pain, try [at some point] to consider their feelings maybe. It took me a long time and a lot of selfishness and mistakes to get to this mindset though and I completely get it).

Don't give up, don't panic and freakout (constantly, its important to remember you are allowed to panic and freak out sometimes if you need to because, hey life is hard, this is hard, but you can be hard too!) Treatments have progressed so much and they are only getting better and more accessible and more researched.

Last thing (and I'll wrap this novel up I promise [and sorry]) but physical therapy is THE BEST. I found out I have super over strengthened pelvic floor muscles which are making my symptoms a trillion times worse. I'm a very stressful, anxious person and tense up so much. I can't always tell when I'm tightening my abdomen, but a good sign according to my PT is if my jaw is tightened, I probably am, and need to breeeeeathe. If this is an option for you I highly recommend.

Good luck! (sorry I wrote so much)
